title: Re-Settlement Figures for a Duplicate Claim Payment, Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan
content:
**The claim.** A second payment of this kind under a Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan is sent as a mailed check, so the claim repaid is the claim of the most recent mailed-check claim payment on the plan; its loss date and peril are read from the claim as filed and its property values are those of the latest adjuster assessment recorded on that claim.

**The re-settled entitlement.** The re-settlement of a duplicate payment takes the general-property value plus each special-class value — jewelry, furs and watches; electronics; collectibles and art; firearms; business inventory — capped at the level's sublimit for that class, caps that sum at the level's coverage limit, and subtracts a deductible equal to the level's deductible, never going below zero, which gives the re-settled entitlement.

**The repayment.** The duplicate repayment is the net claim money paid on the claim — its claim payments less the voids recorded against them — less the re-settled entitlement, never below zero, rounded to the cent only at this final step, and it is recorded against the claim's most recent mailed-check payment.

## Figure flow

| Step | Figure |
| --- | --- |
| claim payments on the claim, less voids | net claim money paid |
| capped class values, summed, capped at the limit, less the deductible | re-settled entitlement |
| net claim money paid less re-settled entitlement, never below zero | duplicate repayment |

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

Level figures assumed: coverage limit 3,200.00, deductible 120.00, collectibles sublimit 650.00. Latest assessment: general property 1,300.00 and collectibles 880.00, the collectibles counted at 650.00: 1,950.00, less 120.00, a re-settled entitlement of 1,830.00. The claim shows a direct deposit of 1,830.00 and a mailed check of 1,830.00, with no void: net 3,660.00. The duplicate repayment is 1,830.00, recorded against the mailed check.
